ManyRequests holds 20 organizations, 44 active client users (plus at least one soft-deleted one still referenced by requests: "Suzy Toth" at Glasswall), 329 requests, 20 invoices, 18 services and 3 brands (all on Physitrack Group). D1 holds 59 organisations, 43 contacts, 35 requests, 11 messages, 124 invoices, 139 invoice items, 9 subscriptions and 4 team members. The two systems barely overlap: D1's 124 invoices all came from the Xero and Stripe importers, not from ManyRequests, and D1's 35 requests are almost entirely seed/junk (Acme Corp, Beta Labs, Gamma Design, "retret", "dsfsd", "ZZ ... delete me") except an 11-row Stride set that was hand-entered and now duplicates 11 real ManyRequests requests. There is NO external-id column anywhere in D1 (no manyrequestsId, externalId or sourceId on any of the 114 tables), so the import has no idempotency key today and must add one before it runs. The biggest safety finding: POST /api/admin/clients emails a portal invite by default (body.sendInvite !== false), and three routes call the Resend REST endpoint directly rather than through lib/email.ts, so an importer that goes through the API layer would mail real clients and a "stub out lib/email.ts" mitigation would not catch all of them. The importer must write rows directly to D1 and touch no route. Team roster: D1 has Liam Miller (super_admin, Clerk-linked) and "Staci Orchard" (super_admin, no Clerk link) plus two invented members (Sarah Chen, James Park) that violate the "don't invent team members" rule; Nathan Day is missing from D1 entirely even though he is a ManyRequests team member and the author of most recent client-facing comments. HOW super_admin IS REPRESENTED (lib/permissions.ts): NOT via team_members.role and NOT via team_members.roles (that column is '[]' for all four). It is a row in team_member_roles joining team_members to roles where roles.name = 'super_admin' and team_member_roles.ended_at IS NULL. The five seeded roles are role-super-admin, role-admin, role-project-manager, role-task-handler, role-viewer. Level resolution at lib/permissions.ts:413 is: super_admin if the role names include 'super_admin', else admin if they include 'admin', else team_member if there is any role at all, else admin for the MCP service token, else (no role anywhere in the workspace) admin as a fresh-install fallback. So Nathan added with no role assignment would land on team_member with an empty viewable-resource set, i.e. deny-all, unless the workspace has zero role assignments (it does not). To give Nathan the 'dev' role he needs a team_member_roles row pointing at role-task-handler (the closest existing role: 'Executes assigned work. Own tasks, comment on requests, log time') or a new 'developer' role; there is no 'dev' role in the roles table today.

INVOICE ITEMS. ManyRequests line_items[] -> D1 invoice_items. name -> description. quantity -> quantity. unit_price -> unit_price_usd (native currency, see above). subtotal -> total_usd. There is no per-line tax column in D1 and ManyRequests carries taxes[] at the invoice level, so a taxed invoice loses its line-level breakdown (all 20 current invoices have taxes[] empty, so this is theoretical today). No manyrequests_id needed if items are always deleted-and-reinserted with their parent, but add one for safety.

SUBSCRIPTIONS / PLANS. ManyRequests organization subscription -> D1 subscriptions. NO ID IS EXPOSED (service name, status, billing_period, member, hours_per_period, credits_per_period, created_at only), so the key is (org manyrequests_id, service name, created_at) -> NEW COLUMN manyrequests_id. status (active|canceled) -> status (active|cancelled). billing_period (Monthly|Quarterly|Annually) -> billing_interval (monthly|quarterly|annually). created_at -> created_at and current_period_start. service name -> plan_type has to be invented: D1's plan_type vocabulary is none|launch|maintain|scale|hourly and ManyRequests sells 'Glasswall Custom Retainer', 'Elevate custom hourly', 'Growth (Design & Dev)' etc. Propose subscriptions.mr_service_name text plus a mapping table, and set plan_type to 'hourly' for the hour-bank retainers and 'scale'/'maintain' for the named plans. hours_per_period and credits_per_period have NO COLUMNS: propose subscriptions.hours_per_period real and credits_per_period real. member (who is billed) -> NO COLUMN: propose subscriptions.billed_contact_id. price and currency have NO COLUMNS on subscriptions at all (D1 keeps money on organisations.custom_mrr / custom_mrr_currency), so per-plan pricing has to be carried on the org or a new column added.

SERVICES / PRICING. ManyRequests service -> D1 `services` table, which EXISTS but has ZERO rows and is not referenced by requests. Before importing requests that name a service, either seed all 18 services (id -> manyrequests_id, name, description, type one-off|recurring, status, currency, price, hours, credits, and pricing_variations[] into a JSON column or a child table) or accept services as a plain text label on requests. pricing_variations{id, price, billing_period, hours, credits, enabled} have no D1 home at all.

BRANDS. ManyRequests organization brand -> D1 has TWO competing representations: a `brands` table (0 rows) and organisations.brands TEXT DEFAULT '[]'. requests.brand_id is a text column with no declared foreign key. Only Physitrack Group has brands (3). Pick the `brands` table (it is the one a brand_id can point at), add manyrequests_id to it, and treat organisations.brands as deprecated, or the three Physitrack brands will exist twice.

MISSING EXTERNAL-ID COLUMNS, ALL OF THEM. A scan of all 114 D1 tables for manyrequest / many_request / external_id / externalId / source_id found NOTHING. 2. PROVE THE GATE, offline, with no network at all. In the worktree: npx vitest run lib/__tests__/email-delivery.test.ts. 33 cases. 3. PROVE THERE IS NO SECOND DOOR. npx vitest run lib/__tests__/no-resend-bypass.test.ts. issues.problem: Clerk organization invitations are a second, entirely ungated mail transport. Three routes call clerk.organizations.createOrganizationInvitation with a caller-supplied address, and Clerk sends its own invitation email from Clerk's systems, so lib/email-delivery.ts never sees it: app/api/admin/team/[id]/invite/route.ts:124 (any Tahi admin, address taken from teamMembers.email), app/api/portal/invites/route.ts:109 and app/api/portal/people/route.ts:136 (any client-org admin, arbitrary address typed in the portal). The no-resend-bypass test only looks for Resend, so it does not catch this. Under the hard rule this is a live path from an authenticated session to a real person's inbox while the studio believes the blackout is total.
issues.fix: Apply the same pure rule before minting the invitation. In each of the three routes, call resolveDeliveryPolicy() + isRecipientAllowed(email, policy, orgId) and, when the address is withheld, write an email_suppressions row (template 'clerk-org-invite') and return 409 with the allowlist reason instead of calling Clerk. Then extend lib/__tests__/no-resend-bypass.test.ts with a fourth rule for createOrganizationInvitation / clerkClient().invitations outside an approved wrapper, so the next one is caught by the test rather than by a reviewer.

issues.problem: Stripe is a second transport that was left open while Xero was closed. The route creates a Stripe customer carrying the client's contact email (line 121), creates an invoice with collection_method: 'send_invoice' (line 153), and then finalizes it (line 171). A finalized send_invoice invoice is emailed to the customer by Stripe itself whenever the account's automatic-collection / 'email finalized invoices' setting is on, and no code here is involved. The route is reachable from the invoice detail page, the invoice list bulk action, and the MCP create_stripe_invoice tool. The identical Xero hole was recognised and stood down in app/api/admin/invoices/[id]/send-email/route.ts; this one was only noted in the handoff, not gated.
issues.fix: Mirror the Xero stand-down. Before stripePost('/invoices', ...), resolve the org's billing contacts, ask partitionRecipients/resolveDeliveryPolicy, and when nothing is allowed either refuse with 409 (allowlist reason) or create the invoice with auto_advance: false and skip the finalize call, logging a suppression row so the hold is provable. Confirm the Stripe account's customer-email setting separately with Liam before the blackout is declared complete.

issues.problem: The gate is domain-level only, so the default policy ['tahi.studio'] permits staci@tahi.studio and nathan@tahi.studio, which Liam named explicitly as addresses that must not be emailed. This is not theoretical: app/api/portal/requests/route.ts fans studioNewRequestEmailPlan out to studio recipients, and lib/notification-email.ts resolveEmailTargets (lines 293-295) resolves those targets straight from teamMembers.email. A client submitting a request or posting a message today mails every team member row, and every tahi.studio one passes the gate.
issues.fix: Add an address-level layer that the domain rule cannot express. Either a new setting email.allowedAddresses (exact mailbox match, plus-alias aware) that must also pass when set, or an email.blockedAddresses denylist checked before the domain rule, seeded with staci@tahi.studio and nathan@tahi.studio. Given the stated rule is 'only Liam's own mailbox until he verifies', the allowlist-of-addresses form is the tighter fit: default it to business@tahi.studio and let the domain list widen it later.

issues.problem: The organisation exemption is evaluated per send, not per address: isRecipientAllowed returns true for ANY address as soon as the send carries an orgId in email.allowedOrgIds. deliverEmail passes the same orgId to the to, cc and bcc partitions, so once a dummy client's org is exempted, an admin sharing a proposal or contract for that org can cc or bcc any address on earth (gmail, a prospect, a competitor) and it is delivered without a suppression row. The exemption is documented as 'a client on an outside domain', but what it actually opens is the whole send.
issues.fix: Scope the exemption to addresses that belong to the exempt org: resolve that org's contacts (or its email domains) and match the recipient against them, rather than returning true unconditionally. At minimum, apply the org exemption only to the `to` partition and keep cc/bcc on the domain rule.

issues.problem: Partial suppression is silently discarded on the success path. deliverEmail is called with the whole body.contactEmails array; if one address is a tahi.studio address and the others are prospects, to.allowed is non-empty, outcome.success is true, and outcome.suppressed is never read. The nudge row keeps status 'sent' and logActivity writes 'Nudge sent to a@prospect.com, b@tahi.studio' naming recipients who received nothing. The same shape exists in the share routes, which do collect outcome.suppressed but return it alongside a per-signer 'sent' entry.
issues.fix: Read outcome.suppressed on the success path too. Return suppressed (and suppressedCount) in the response, and make the timeline entry name only outcome.delivered, so the deal history never claims a recipient the gate withheld. Same one-line change in the contract/proposal/schedule share routes: build the sent list from outcome.delivered rather than from the loop variable.

issues.problem: The single most dangerous write in the system is the least protected. PATCH /api/admin/settings gates only on isTahiAdmin, so any member of the Tahi Clerk org, and the MCP service token (which resolves to admin), can set email.deliveryMode to 'all' and open delivery to every address. No requireFeature('settings'), no super_admin check, and no audit row is written. By contrast DELETE /api/admin/email-suppressions requires super_admin. The MCP tool description tells the model not to do it, which is a prompt, not a guard.
issues.fix: Gate the three email.* keys behind resolvePermissions(...).isSuperAdmin in the PATCH handler (the same check the suppressions DELETE uses), and write a logAudit entry on every deliveryMode change recording old value, new value and actor. The UI ConfirmDialog stays as the human-facing half; this is the half an MCP client cannot talk its way past.

issues.problem: recipientDomain judges a recipient string by the text after its LAST '@'. That correctly defeats a quoted local part, but it also means a single string holding several addresses is judged by the last one: 'a@acme.com, b@tahi.studio' resolves to tahi.studio, passes, and is handed to Resend verbatim. The share and nudge routes accept recipient strings from the API body and from MCP without checking that each entry is one address (the settings UI uses input type=email per row, so the UI path is safe, but the API path is not).
issues.fix: Reject rather than parse: in partitionRecipients, treat an address as unparseable (and therefore withheld) when it contains a comma, a semicolon, internal whitespace outside a display name, or more than one '@' after the angle-bracket form is unwrapped. It fails in the safe direction and costs one regex.

issues.problem: Three routes still return early when RESEND_API_KEY is absent (proposals line 49, and the equivalent guards in the contract and schedule share routes), and the deal nudge wraps its whole send in `if (process.env.RESEND_API_KEY)`. In a key-less environment those paths produce no suppression rows, which undercuts the design property the gate is built on: that the filter and the log run before the key is looked at, so the blackout is provable without mailing anyone.
issues.fix: Move the key check inside deliverEmail's remit (it already returns 'RESEND_API_KEY not configured' after filtering and logging) and delete the early returns, so a key-less dry run still leaves an evidence trail for every address it would have withheld.

issues.problem: cc and bcc are partitioned once per `to` inside the per-signer loop, so a withheld cc address produces one email_suppressions row and one `suppressed` array entry per signer. A three-signer contract with one blocked cc writes three identical rows and returns the address three times, which makes the log read as three withheld sends when there was one. Same shape in the proposal and schedule routes.
issues.fix: Partition cc/bcc once before the loop and pass only the surviving lists into deliverEmail, or dedupe the collected `suppressed` array before returning it and before writing rows.

issues.problem: resolveDeliveryPolicy does an unfiltered SELECT of the entire settings table on every single send. An announcement fan-out (lib/announcement-emails.ts sends one email per contact, in slices) therefore issues one full settings read per recipient, plus one insert per withheld recipient.
issues.fix: Either filter the select to the three keys with inArray, or let deliverEmail accept an optional pre-resolved policy so a fan-out reads it once and passes it down. The announcement and notification fan-outs are the two call sites that need it.
